## Company: DDMP REIT, Inc. (DDMPR)
Sector: Property / Property
DDMP REIT, Inc. (DDMPR) was incorporated on October 27, 2014, as a real estate company primarily to construct DD Meridian Park, a 4.75 hectare mixed-use development situated in Pasay City. 

The Company is a real estate investment trust formed primarily to own and invest in an income producing commercial portfolio of office, retail, industrial and hotel properties in the Philippines that meet its investment criteria for Grade A, centrally located, stably occupied, and income producing properties. The Company's sponsor is DoubleDragon Properties Corp. 

DDMPR's property portfolio consists of three commercial properties in DD Meridian Park. These are DoubleDragon Plaza, DoubleDragon Center East, and DoubleDragon Center West. The land on which these buildings are built forms part of the Company's asset portfolio and is owned by the Company. As of December 31, 2024, the Company's portfolio comprised approximately 172,252 square meters of gross leasable area.

Source: SEC Form 17-A (2024)

thesis:
Enough data. Writing thesis now.

---

DDMP REIT is a straightforward business to understand: it owns and operates three commercial office buildings — DoubleDragon Plaza, DD Center East, and DD Center West — sitting on 172,252 hectares of gross leasable area inside DD Meridian Park in Pasay City's Bay Area. The income model is simple: collect rent, distribute to shareholders. There is nothing here that strains the circle of competence.

The moat, however, is thin. DDMPR's only real competitive advantage is location — the Bay Area and MOA Entertainment Complex corridor is a legitimate draw for BPO and corporate tenants — but it is not irreplaceable. Office REITs globally face structural headwinds from hybrid work arrangements, and the portfolio's own data exposes this: DD Center East sits at roughly 6.6% occupancy as of early 2026, while DD Plaza manages only 73.7%. That a building included in the REIT's IPO asset pool remains essentially empty years into operation is a damning signal about tenant demand for this specific product in this specific location. DD Center West at 95.2% shows the location can work, but it also highlights how uneven the portfolio is. There is no switching-cost moat, no network effect, and no pricing power beyond what the Bay Area market will bear.

Management presents a mixed picture. The debt-free balance sheet is a genuine positive and a structural advantage most Philippine office REITs lack — it eliminates refinancing risk, keeps distributable income high, and provides flexibility to acquire new assets without diluting equity at a depressed share price. The decision to hike dividends after strong earnings (Q1 net income +24.7% to ₱3.88B, revenue +20.5% to ₱4.52B) signals shareholder-friendly intent. But the lingering near-zero occupancy at DD Center East — an asset that should have been stabilized before being injected into the REIT — reflects either optimistic underwriting, weak leasing execution, or both. The sponsor, DoubleDragon Properties Corp., has a history of ambitious timelines that slip. That pattern matters when evaluating whether management's stated three-year portfolio diversification plan will deliver.

On valuation, the numbers are superficially compelling. At ₱1.03, DDMPR trades at 6.1x trailing earnings and just 0.3x book — deeply discounted by any conventional screen. The 9.3% dividend yield is real income being paid today, backed by a debt-free entity. But the ten-year underlying trend remains sobering: revenue down 3.4% annually, earnings down 5.3%, and EPS shrinking at 14.6% over the decade despite book value growing 17% annually (a divergence that suggests equity dilution or retained earnings not translating into earning power). The 2025 rebound is encouraging but insufficient to override the long structural drift. The Sticker Price is not calculable with confidence given the erratic growth history, which itself is a warning: durable compounders are predictable. DDMPR has not been.

The core tension is this: at ₱1.03, you are buying real assets at 30 cents on the book-value dollar with a near-10% cash yield, zero debt, and a potential catalyst if DD Center East ever fills. That is a legitimate deep-value setup. But it is a value trap if occupancy stagnates, the BPO sector softens further, or management deploys capital poorly in its acquisition pipeline. The margin of safety on assets is real; the margin of safety on earnings power is not.

At the current price, DDMPR is a **watch**. The high yield and debt-free structure limit downside, but the unresolved DD Center East occupancy problem is the key question the market is right to discount. If occupancy at East climbs above 50% over the next two to three quarters — demonstrable evidence that leasing momentum has turned — that becomes a credible buy trigger at current or lower prices. Until then, collect no dividend you have not earned through conviction on the business, and let the execution story prove itself.
